correctness.rationale: For the repaired claim, the killed Brownian resolvent on the positive interval is the difference of two free resolvents. Multiplying by r gives the interrupted-position measure; conditioning on the terminal attempt cancels the common direct-capture factor e^(−z) in the odds. The interior-positive sinh kernel is strictly increasing in z and grows unboundedly on any interior subinterval with positive lower bound on the splitting profile. Its entire Taylor coefficients, under u=(1−y)^2, determine a compact signed measure by polynomial density. Distinct rates accumulating even at zero suffice by the identity theorem. The repaired interior-reference scale derivative verifies the drift reconstruction for continuous interior drift without assuming an integral from 0. For finitely many readings, their homogeneous functionals have a nonzero null vector in the endpoint-vanishing polynomial space of dimension one more than the number of readings; small signed perturbations preserve both strictly positive derivatives and strictly positive second derivatives of the base profile, hence give different inward drifts with the same data. The neutral formula follows by integrating the linear profile, and the negative-side first hitting time gives infinite mean without jeopardizing eventual capture. The frozen numerical value for z_* squared contains an incorrect last displayed digit; the corrected files use the independently obtained 4.740717962290353…, and the checker now bisects instead of printing a hard-coded root to unjustified precision. No theorem hypotheses or inverse-observation channel were changed.
residual_risks: The bounded tests corroborate the neutral example only; monotonicity and inverse results depend on the analytic proofs. No supplied full script was executed.

Closest forward and inverse sources in the originality assessment
value.rationale: A single binary terminal label is a much coarser observation than a return trajectory or MFPT profile. The theorem says exactly which continuous response data recover the positive-interval force and proves why arbitrary finitely many noiseless readings cannot do so, even with smooth strict inward motion. Strict crossover and the neutral benchmark give checkable consequences independent of whether completion has finite mean.
residual_risks: No noise-stable or finite-sample drift estimator, no recovery of negative-side dynamics, and no identification of unknown diffusivity are established.
